Below is a structured 12-week strength program for a 30-year-old advanced lifter at 20 weeks pregnant, with medical clearance for moderate strength and the specified contraindications (no supine after week 16, no max attempts, no contact sports). The plan emphasizes safety, progressive overload within comfortable limits, and exercise selections that accommodate a growing belly and changing biomechanics. It assumes access to a full gym (machines, free weights, cables). Adjustments should be made in real-time based on comfort, symptoms, and medical guidance.

Key considerations and safety notes
- RPE and perceived exertion: Aim for RPE 6–7/10 on most sets (moderate intensity). If any red-flag symptoms (dizziness, chest pain, shortness of breath, leakage, vaginal bleeding, severe pelvic/abdominal pain), stop and consult a clinician.
- Positioning: No supine exercises after 16 weeks. Favor seated, incline, standing, or supported positions (incline bench, back-supported machine, seated leg press). For core work, avoid valgus collapsing movements that increase intra-abdominal pressure and avoid supine positions after mid-pregnancy.
- Breathing: Use a controlled breathing pattern; exhale on exertion, avoid Valsalva for long durations. If needed, shorten set length and use breath holds only with guidance.
- Load and progression: Prioritize technique and intra-set quality over loading. Increase load conservatively (2–5% or 1–2 reps) when form is solid and there are no symptoms.
- Core and pelvic floor: Integrate diastasis-aware and pelvic floor-conscious cues. Avoid high-load overhead press if it causes rib flare or core instability. Include gentle abdominal and pelvic floor engagement cues.
- Recovery: Ensure adequate sleep, hydration, and nutrition. Consider additional protein intake aligned with prenatal guidelines (discuss with client’s clinician). Include mobility and diaphragmatic breathing as part of warm-up and cool-down.

Program structure
- Frequency: 4 training days per week (2 upper-lift days, 2 lower-lift days) with one optional light cardio or mobility day. This keeps sessions manageable and supports strength without excessive fatigue.
- Phases: 3 phases of 4 weeks each (Phase 1: foundational conditioning and technique, Phase 2: progressive overload and volume slightly increased, Phase 3: peak strength with controlled intensification) plus deload and recovery considerations at the end of each phase.
- Weekly outline (example): 
  - Monday: Upper Body Strength A
  - Tuesday: Lower Body Strength A
  - Thursday: Upper Body Strength B
  - Friday: Lower Body Strength B
  - Optional: Mobility/Light cardio session mid-week or on rest days

12-week plan details

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation, technique, and safe strength base
Goals: Establish technique with moderate loads, build pelvic floor and core engagement, accommodate pregnancy changes, and set a sustainable weekly routine.

Weekly template
- Warm-up: 8–10 minutes light cardio (rowing, bike, elliptical) + dynamic mobility for hips, shoulders, thoracic spine. Include diaphragmatic breathing and 2–3 spine-safe warm-up sets per major lift.
- Core/pelvic floor: 5 minutes daily activation (Kegels, gentle transverse abdominis activation), 2–3 times per week integrated into warm-up or between sets.

Upper Body Strength A (Weeks 1–4)
1) Dumbbell bench press or incline press (no supine after week 16; incline is acceptable)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
   - Notes: Maintain scapular retraction, feet stable. If incline causes rib discomfort, switch to seated dumbbell press or machine chest press.

2) Seated one-arm dumbbell row (or supported machine row)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10 per side
   - Rest: 90 seconds

3) Seated or supported overhead press (DB or safe machine)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
   - Cues: Keep ribs down, avoid arching the back. If pressing behind the head is uncomfortable, use a neutral-grip or Arnold press variation within comfort.

4) Lat pulldown or low-row with cable
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds

5) Lateral raises (light)
   - Sets: 2
   - Reps: 12–15
   - Rest: 60 seconds
   - Cues: Keep movement controlled, minimal inertia.

6) Core/anti-rotation 2–3 sets
   - Pallof press with resistance band or cable, 8–10 reps per side, 2–3 sets
   - Side planks: hold 15–25 seconds per side if comfortable; avoid if pressure or diastasis symptoms.

Lower Body Strength A (Weeks 1–4)
1) Goblet squat or front-loaded goblet squat
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 90 seconds
   - Cues: Weight in heels, torso upright, avoid deep flexion if uncomfortable.

2) Romanian deadlift with dumbbells (maintain neutral spine)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
   - Cues: Hinge at hips, not rounding back.

3) Leg press or leg extension/clex
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 90 seconds

4) Glute bridges or hip thrust (supported, avoid excessive arching)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 12–15
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds

5) Hamstring curls or Nordic ham curls alternative
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds

6) Core: dead bug or bird-dog
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 8–10 per side
   - Rest: 60 seconds

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive overload with safer intensification
Goals: Increase training density and challenge while staying within comfort. Reduce risk by using hypertrophy-range rep schemes and maintained technique.

Upper Body Strength B (Weeks 5–8)
1) Dumbbell floor press or incline bench press (if floor press allowed; no supine beyond 16 weeks—Floor press is semi-supine; ensure safe positioning)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
   - Note: If floor press is uncomfortable, use incline machine press.

2) Seated cable row or chest-supported row
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds

3) Dumbbell push press (no jerk, controlled)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Rest: 90 seconds
   - Cues: Use legs for drive with minimal lumbar extension

4) Face pulls
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 12–15
   - Rest: 60 seconds

5) Cable lateral raises
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 12–15
   - Rest: 60 seconds

6) Core: anti-rotation or pallof variations
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 8–10 per side
   - Rest: 60 seconds

Lower Body Strength B (Weeks 5–8)
1) Back-supported barbell or dumbbell squat (upright posture, may use safety bar or Smith machine)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
   - Cues: Maintain neutral spine, depth comfortable.

2) Romanian deadlift or hinge to mid-shin with moderate load
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds

3) Walking lunges or reverse lunges (short step to keep balance)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10 per leg
   - Rest: 90 seconds

4) Leg press or hack squat
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 90 seconds

5) Glute bridges or hip thrusts with tempo (2–0-2-0)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 12–15
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds

6) Core and pelvic floor: side planks with leg lift (if comfortable)
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 8–10 per side
   - Rest: 60 seconds

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak strength with sustainable load and recovery emphasis
Goals: Maintain gains, optimize form, and ensure readiness for postnatal training normalization.

Upper Body Strength C (Weeks 9–12)
1) Barbell or dumbbell overhead press (if allowed; safer alternative: machine shoulder press)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 5–6
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
   - Cues: Use legs to drive if needed; avoid lumbar arch.

2) Dumbbell bench press or incline press
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds

3) Seated cable row or chest-supported row
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds

4) Lat pulldown with supination grip
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 60–90 seconds

5) Upright row or cable face pulls for traps/ rear delts
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 60 seconds

6) Core: dead bug progressions or bird-dogs with resistance bands
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 8–10 per side
   - Rest: 60 seconds

Lower Body Strength C (Weeks 9–12)
1) Front squat or goblet squat variation (if front squat uncomfortable, maintain goblet)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds

2) Hip hinge progression: hex bar deadlift or conventional dumbbell Romanian deadlift
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Rest: 90 seconds

3) Bulgarian split squat (supported if balance is an issue)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8 per leg
   - Rest: 90 seconds

4) Leg press or measured lunge
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds

5) Glute bridges or hip thrusts with tempo
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 10–12
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds

6) Core: Pallof press or standing cable anti-rotation
   - Sets: 2–3
   - Reps: 8–10 per side
   - Rest: 60 seconds

Deload and recovery
- Week 4, Week 8, Week 12 should include a deload: reduce volume by 30–40% and maintain intensity at 6–7/10 for safe adaptation.
- Emphasize mobility and diaphragmatic breathing during deload weeks.
- Incorporate pelvic floor/quadruped breathing drills on rest days.

Optional cardio and conditioning
- 2–3 days per week: 20–30 minutes of moderate-intensity cardio (stationary bike, brisk walking, swimming if comfortable) or low-impact intervals (1–2 minutes easy, 1 minute moderate) depending on energy and symptoms.
- Focus on staying active, not chasing high cardio performance during pregnancy.

Nutrition and recovery guidance
- Protein: Aim for roughly 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day depending on appetite and clinician advice; adjust for trimester and energy needs.
- Hydration: 2–3 liters per day or as advised, especially around training.
- Meals: Balanced meals with adequate carbohydrates around workouts to support performance and fetal needs.
- Supplements: Follow OB/GYN guidance on prenatal vitamins, iron, calcium, and any other prescribed supplements.
- Sleep and stress: Prioritize sleep, limit high-stress activities, and consider a short post-workout mobility routine to aid recovery.

Monitoring and progression notes
- Sessions should be adjusted based on fatigue, nausea, heartburn, or pelvic discomfort. If any exercise causes discomfort or symptoms worsen, modify or substitute with a safer alternative (e.g., switch to machine-based movements, reduce range of motion, or pause for that day).
- All exercises chosen should prioritize stable spine and safe shoulder and knee joints. Avoid supine positions after 16 weeks; if any exercise historically performed supine (e.g., bench press), switch to incline or machine chest press or dumbbell floor press with careful technique and clinician approval.
- If diastasis recti signs appear or worsen (doming, bulging with core engagement), adjust core work to more supportive, intra-abdominal pressure-friendly movements and consult a clinician.

Sample 1-week microcycle (Weeks 5–8 example)
- Monday: Upper Body Strength B
  1) Seated cable row: 3x8–10
  2) Dumbbell incline bench press: 3x6–8
  3) Dumbbell push press: 3x6–8
  4) Face pulls: 3x12–15
  5) Cable lateral raises: 2x12–15
  6) Pallof press: 2–3x8–10 per side

- Tuesday: Lower Body Strength B
  1) Back-supported squat: 3x6–8
  2) Romanian deadlift: 3x8–10
  3) Walking lunges: 3x8–10 per leg
  4) Leg press: 3x10–12
  5) Glute bridges: 3x12–15
  6) Side planks: 2x20–30 seconds per side

- Thursday: Upper Body Strength A (earlier phase)
  1) Dumbbell bench press: 3x8–10
  2) Seated one-arm row: 3x8–10 per side
  3) Seated overhead press: 3x8–10
  4) Lat pulldown: 3x10–12
  5) Lateral raises: 2x12–15
  6) Pallof/band anti-rotation: 2–3x8–10 per side

- Friday: Lower Body Strength A
  1) Goblet squat: 3x10–12
  2) Hip hinge to mid-shin: 3x8–10
  3) Goblet step-down or stepping squats: 3x8–10 per leg
  4) Hamstring curls or stability hamstring machine: 3x10–12
  5) Glute bridges: 3x12–15
  6) Dead bug: 2–3x8–10 per side

Communication with client and clinician
- Check in weekly for symptom changes, energy, nausea, or any discomfort patterns.
- Maintain open dialogue about exercise modifications and progression tolerances.
- If any red flags appear, pause training and consult the client’s obstetric care provider.

- Fats: Include healthy fats for caloric density and essential fatty acids (omega-3s) important for fetal development.

Below is a cohesive, 12-week prenatal strength program for a 20-week pregnant, advanced lifter who has OB clearance for moderate strength. The plan respects the contraindications you provided (no supine after week 16, no max attempts, no contact sports) and integrates the adjustments discussed: explicit upper-body pressing options (bench press adaptations), phase-based progression with Phase 2 intensity, integrated cardio tailored to pregnancy, comprehensive core work with diastasis/pelvic-floor considerations, and a safe peak-week approach in Week 12 that avoids true 1RM testing.

How to read this plan
- Frequency: 4 dedicated lifting days per week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B) with 2 optional cardio/mobility days. On weeks when energy is limited, you can swap a lifting day for mobility/conditioning.
- Phases: 3 phases, each 4 weeks (Phase 1 weeks 1–4; Phase 2 weeks 5–8; Phase 3 weeks 9–12). Deloads are incorporated within Week 4, Week 8, and Week 12 as described.
- Progression: Emphasis on RPE targets, tempo (time under tension), submax loads, and technique. No max efforts and no supine loading after 16 weeks.
- Exercise substitutions: All pressing work is adapted to avoid full supine loading; incline, floor press variants, seated presses, or machine presses are used.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation, technique, safe base with core and cardio integration
Goals
- Build technique and pelvic-floor engagement.
- Establish a sustainable training rhythm; normalize breathing and core activation.
- Introduce cardio in a controlled manner; maintain lean-mass goals through adequate protein and calories.

Weekly layout
- Monday: Upper A
- Tuesday: Lower A
- Thursday: Upper B
- Friday: Lower B
- Optional: Cardio/Mobility 1–2 days (midweek)

Warm-up (every lifting day)
- 8–10 minutes light cardio (rower, bike, elliptical) at easy pace.
- Dynamic mobility: hips, thoracic spine, shoulders; activate diaphragmatic breathing; 2–3 warm-up sets per major lift.

Core baseline (daily, 5–6 minutes)
- Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor activation (2–3 sets of 5 breaths; exhale with pelvic floor engagement).
- Dead bugs or dead-bug progressions: 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps per side.
- Bird-dog: 2–3 sets of 8–10 reps per side.
- Pallof press (light, if tolerated): 2–3 sets of 8–10 per side.

Phase 1: detailed weekly programming

Upper A (Weeks 1–4)
1) Incline dumbbell press or machine incline press
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
   - Notes: Upright posture; scapular retraction; rib cage stable. If rib discomfort, switch to seated dumbbell press.
2) Seated one-arm dumbbell row (or supported machine row)
   - 3x8–10 per side
   - Rest: 90 seconds
3) Seated or neutral-grip overhead press
   - 3x8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
4) Lat pulldown or low-row
   - 3x10–12
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds
5) Lateral raises
   - 2x12–15
   - Rest: 60 seconds
6) Core/anti-rotation
   - Pallof press: 2–3x8–10 per side
   - Side planks: 15–25 seconds per side (if comfortable)

Lower A (Weeks 1–4)
1) Goblet squat or front-loaded goblet squat
   - 3x10–12
   - 90 seconds
2) Romanian deadlift with dumbbells
   - 3x8–10
   - 90 seconds
3) Leg press or leg extension
   - 3x10–12
   - 90 seconds
4) Glute bridges or hip thrust (supported)
   - 3x12–15
   - 60–75 seconds
5) Hamstring curls or Nordic alternatives
   - 2–3x10–12
   - 60–75 seconds
6) Core: dead bug or bird-dog
   - 2–3x8–10 per side

Upper B (Weeks 1–4)
- Because this is still Phase 1, the emphasis is technique and comfortable loads. You can repeat a pattern similar to Upper A with adjustments for variety.
1) Seated dumbbell floor press or incline floor press (if tolerated)
   - 3x8–10
   - 90 seconds
2) Seated cable row or chest-supported row
   - 3x8–10
   - 90 seconds
3) Seated overhead press (neutral grip)
   - 3x8–10
   - 90 seconds
4) Lat pulldown
   - 3x10–12
   - 60–75 seconds
5) Face pulls
   - 2–3x12–15
   - 60 seconds
6) Pallof press
   - 2–3x8–10 per side

Lower B (Weeks 1–4)
1) Back-supported squat (safety rack or Smith machine if preferred)
   - 3x8–10
   - 90 seconds
2) Romanian deadlift
   - 3x8–10
   - 90 seconds
3) Walking lunges or reverse lunges
   - 3x8–10 per leg
   - 90 seconds
4) Leg press or hack squat
   - 3x10–12
   - 90 seconds
5) Glute bridges or hip thrusts
   - 3x12–15
   - 60–75 seconds
6) Side planks (or modification)
   - 2–3x20–30 seconds per side

Cardio (Weeks 1–4)
- 2 cardio sessions per week
  - Session A: 20–25 minutes brisk walk or easy cycling; include 2–3 minutes moderate pace every 5 minutes if comfortable
  - Session B: 20–25 minutes swimming or pool-based cardio if available

Phase 1 deload (Week 4)
- Reduce volume by ~30–40% across lifting days; maintain technique. Keep cardio light to moderate.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Push intensity, maintain safety, raise perceived effort, keep “training hard” feeling
Goals
- Increase density and controlled fatigue with tempo work and heavier loads within safe ranges.
- Emphasize pressing stimulus (bench-pressing enthusiasm) via floor/ incline/ machine press variations.
- Maintain core, pelvic-floor integrity, and diastasis precautions.

Weekly layout
- Monday: Upper B
- Tuesday: Lower B
- Thursday: Upper A
- Friday: Lower A
- Optional: Cardio/Mobility 2–3 days

Upper B (Weeks 5–8)
1) Floor press or incline press
   - Sets: 4
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Tempo: 3–0–1–0
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
   - RPE target: 7–8 on work sets
   - Notes: Floor press favored if supine tolerance is limited; incline press if rib comfort allows.
2) Seated cable row or chest-supported row
   - 4x8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
3) Dumbbell push press
   - 4x6–8
   - Tempo: 2–0–1–0
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
4) Face pulls
   - 3x12–15
   - Rest: 60 seconds
5) Cable lateral raises
   - 3x12–15
   - Rest: 60 seconds
6) Pallof press with hold
   - 3x8–10 per side
   - Hold: 2–3 seconds at peak tension

Lower B (Weeks 5–8)
1) Back-supported squat (safety rack/Safety bar)
   - 4x6–8
   - Tempo: 3–0–1–0
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
2) Romanian deadlift or hinge to mid-shin
   - 4x8–10
   - Tempo: 2–0–2–0
   - Rest: 90 seconds
3) Walking lunges or reverse lunges
   - 3–4x8–10 per leg
   - Tempo: 2–0–2–0
   - Rest: 90 seconds
4) Leg press or hack squat
   - 3–4x10–12
   - Tempo: 2–0–2–0
5) Glute bridges or hip thrusts with tempo
   - 3x12–15
   - Tempo: 3–0–2–0
6) Side planks or modified core
   - 2–3x20–30 seconds per side
   - Rest: 60 seconds

Cardio (Weeks 5–8)
- Maintain 2–3 cardio sessions per week
  - Session A: 25–30 minutes cycling with 4–5 x 2-minute moderate intervals, rest 2 minutes easy
  - Session B: 30 minutes brisk walk or aquatic cardio; incline added if feasible
  - Optional Session C: 15–20 minutes low-intensity cardio (swim, aqua aerobics)

Phase 2 deload (Week 8)
- Reduce volume by ~30–40%; reduce sets on main lifts by 1 and reduce accessory load; keep tempos.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak week with deliberate testing approach that avoids true 1RM
Goals
- Preserve gains, maintain safe peak-week stimulus, and provide a test-like metric without maxing out.
- Continue with strong pressing presence, robust core work, and controlled loading.

Weekly layout
- Monday: Upper C
- Tuesday: Lower C
- Thursday: Upper A or B (rotate)
- Friday: Lower A or B
- Cardio: 2–3 days as tolerated

Upper C (Weeks 9–12)
1) Dumbbell bench press or incline bench press (seated or machine press if needed)
   - Sets: 3
   - Reps: 6–8
   - Tempo: 2–0–1–0
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
   - RPE: 7–8
2) Seated cable row or chest-supported row
   - 3x8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
3) Overhead press (machine or dumbbell, seated)
   - 3x6–8
   - Rest: 90 seconds
4) Lat pulldown
   - 2–3x8–10
   - Rest: 60–90 seconds
5) Upright row or face pulls
   - 2–3x10–12
   - Rest: 60 seconds
6) Core: Pallof press or dead bug variants
   - 3x8–10 per side

Lower C (Weeks 9–12)
1) Front squat or goblet squat
   - 3x6–8
   - Tempo: 2–0–1–0
   - Rest: 90–120 seconds
2) Hip hinge progression: hex bar deadlift or dumbbell RDL
   - 3x6–8
   - Rest: 90 seconds
3) Bulgarian split squat (supported if balance is an issue)
   - 3x6–8 per leg
   - Rest: 90 seconds
4) Leg press or measured lunge
   - 3x8–10
   - Rest: 90 seconds
5) Glute bridges or hip thrusts
   - 3x10–12
   - Rest: 60–75 seconds
6) Core: Pallof press or standing anti-rotation
   - 2–3x8–10 per side

Peak Week testing options (Week 12; no true 1RM)
- Do not attempt a 1RM. Use one of the following:
  Option A: Repetition-based top set (no failure)
    - After a full warm-up, perform 1 top set on 1 primary lift (incline press or floor press) for 3–5 reps with a challenging but controlled load. Record load and reps; do not exceed this effort.
  Option B: RM estimation within safe bounds
    - Choose a 3–4RM or 5–6RM on primary lifts with pristine technique; do not attempt to extend beyond the target reps.
  Option C: Velocity-based surrogate (if equipment available)
    - Lift a submax load to a prescribed velocity zone to gauge progress, not maxing out.
  Option D: Movement-based performance metric
    - Non-load test such as a fixed number of tempo squats with a comfortable load or a bench-inclined push movement performed for max controlled reps (not to failure).

Post-peak progression (Weeks 13+)
- Transition to a gentler deload and maintenance plan focusing on mobility, core stability, and gradual reintroduction of more neutral core workouts post-partum planning.
- You can reintroduce more direct core work and progressive resistance training after an OB clearance signal and comfortable progression.

General safety, cues, and adjustments
- Red flags: chest pain, dizziness, severe shortness of breath, vaginal bleeding, leakage, severe pelvic or abdominal pain. Stop and seek evaluation.
- Breathing: avoid long valsalva; exhale on exertion; maintain diaphragmatic engagement and gentle intra-abdominal pressure.
- Positioning: avoid supine after 16 weeks. Use incline, seated, or supported variations for pressing and leg work.
- Pelvic floor: avoid bearing down; cue pelvic floor engagement on every rep.
- Diastasis: watch for doming or bulging; adjust core work to TVA bracing and anti-rotation movements as needed.

Nutrition and cardio integration (summary)
- Maintain protein target around 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day.
- Calorie surplus: moderate, aligned with third-trimester needs and activity level (adjust per weight gain and clinician guidance).
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 liters per day, more on training days.
- Cardio: 2–3 days/week in Phase 1; 2–3 days in Phase 2; 3 days in Phase 3 as tolerated, with emphasis on RPE 4–6/10, 20–45 minutes per session.
- Food safety: avoid high-mercury fish, raw eggs/meats, unpasteurized dairy, etc., and follow prenatal vitamins.

Core integration notes
- Core work is woven into and around lifting days; core should be practiced on most days (3–5 days/week) with short sessions to support pelvic stability and diastasis concerns.
